bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第153卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 153
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 153

sentences.zh: 【梁紀九】　屠維作噩，一年。

translations.literal: Liang Records 9 — year one of the sexagenary cycle jiyou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Records, Part 9 — the first year of the reign era Zhongdatong.

sentences.zh: ◎中大通元己酉，公元五二九年

translations.literal: ◎ Zhongdatong 1, jiyou, CE 529.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Zhongdatong 1, year jiyou, 529 CE.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅，魏於暉所部都督彭樂師二千餘騎叛，奔韓樓，暉引還。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day jiayin, more than two thousand horsemen under Commander Peng Le of Yu Hui's command in Wei rebelled and fled to Han Lou; Yu Hui withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's jiayin day, over two thousand horsemen led by the commander Peng Le in Yu Hui's Wei detachment mutinied and defected to Han Lou, and Yu Hui pulled his forces back.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, the Emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice and issued a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏汝南王悅求還國，許之。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, the Prince of Runan in Wei, Yuan Yue, asked to return to his fief; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Wei Prince of Runan, Yuan Yue, petitioned to return to his domain, and the court allowed it.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，上祀明堂。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, the Emperor sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the emperor offered sacrifice at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲午，魏主尊彭城武宣王為文穆皇帝，廟號肅祖；

translations.literal: In the second month, on day jiawu, the Wei ruler honored the Prince of Pengcheng, posthumous name Wuxuan, as Emperor Wenmu, with temple name Suzu;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiawu, the Wei emperor posthumously elevated Prince Wuxuan of Pengcheng as Emperor Wenmu, with the temple name Suzu;

sentences.zh: 母李妃為文穆皇后。

translations.literal: his mother, Consort Li, as Empress Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Li, was honored as Empress Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 將遷神主於太廟，以高祖為伯考，大司馬兼錄尚書臨淮王彧表諫，以為：「漢高祖立太上皇廟於香街，光武祀南頓君於舂陵。

translations.literal: When they were about to move the spirit tablets to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and treat Emperor Gaozu as an uncle in the patriline, the Grand Marshal and Acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, memorialized in protest, saying: "Emperor Gaozu of Han established the temple of the Supreme Emperor at Xiang Street, and Emperor Guangwu enshrined his father at Chunling.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to install their spirit tablets in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and rank Emperor Gaozu as a collateral forebear, the Grand Marshal and acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, submitted a memorial of protest: "Emperor Gaozu of Han raised a temple to the Supreme Emperor on Fragrant Street, and Emperor Guangwu worshipped his father at Chunling.

sentences.zh: 元帝之於光武，已疏絕服，猶身奉子道，入繼大宗。

translations.literal: Between Emperor Yuan and Emperor Guangwu the bond of mourning was already severed, yet Guangwu still personally observed the son's rites and entered to succeed the great lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Between Emperor Yuan and Emperor Guangwu the mourning tie was already distant, yet Guangwu still personally kept a son's duty and entered the succession of the great lineage.

sentences.zh: 高祖德洽寰中，道超無外，肅祖雖勳格宇宙，猶北面為臣。

translations.literal: Our Gaozu's virtue filled the realm and his Way surpassed all bounds; though Suzu's merit reached to heaven and earth, he still faced north as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Our Gaozu's virtue filled the realm and his Way surpassed all within the four seas; though Suzu's achievements spanned the cosmos, he still stood facing north as a subject.

sentences.zh: 又，二後皆將配享，乃是君臣並筵，嫂叔同室，竊謂不可。

translations.literal: Moreover, both empresses are to receive joint sacrifice—this would set lord and minister at one mat and sister-in-law with brother-in-law in one chamber; I venture that it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, both empresses are to share the altar—lord and minister would sit at one feast, sister-in-law and brother-in-law under one roof; this, I submit, cannot be allowed.

sentences.zh: 」吏部尚書李神俊亦諫，不聽，彧又請去「帝」著「皇」，亦不聽。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Personnel Li Shenjun also remonstrated, but they were not heeded; Yuan Yu again asked to drop the character "emperor" and use only "august," and this too was refused.
translations.idiomatic: " The Minister of Personnel, Li Shenjun, remonstrated as well, but the throne would not listen; Yuan Yu then asked that the title drop "emperor" and read only "august," and that too was refused.

sentences.zh: 詔更定二百四十號將軍為四十四班。

translations.literal: An edict reorganized the two hundred forty general ranks into forty-four grades.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reorganized the two hundred forty general officer titles into forty-four grades.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏詔濟陰王暉業兼行台尚書，都督丘大千等鎮梁國。

translations.literal: On day renyin, Wei ordered Prince Ye of Jiyin to act as Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the mobile staff and to command Qiu Daqian and others in garrisoning the Liang region.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wei ordered Prince Ye of Jiyin to serve concurrently as acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the mobile staff and to place Qiu Daqian and others in command of the Liang region.

sentences.zh: 暉業，小新成之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Ye was a great-grandson of the Lesser Xin Prince Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was a great-grandson of the Lesser Xin Prince Cheng.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬戌，魏詔上黨王天穆討邢杲，以費穆為前鋒大都督。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day renxu, Wei ordered the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, to campaign against Xing Luo, with Fei Mu as Grand Commander of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renxu, Wei ordered the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, to suppress Xing Luo, appointing Fei Mu grand commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，魏遷肅祖及文穆皇后神主於太廟，又追尊彭城王劭為孝宣皇帝。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on day guiwei, Wei moved the spirit tablets of Suzu and Empress Wenmu to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and further posthumously honored Prince Shao of Pengcheng as Emperor Xiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guiwei, Wei installed the spirit tablets of Suzu and Empress Wenmu in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and further posthumously honored Prince Shao of Pengcheng as Emperor Xiaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧諫曰：「茲事古所未有，陛下作而不法，後世何觀！

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, remonstrated, saying: "Such a thing has never existed in antiquity. Your Majesty acts without precedent—what will posterity think!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, remonstrated: "Nothing like this exists in antiquity. Your Majesty acts without precedent—what will later ages make of it!"

sentences.zh: 」弗聽。

translations.literal: They were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 魏元天穆將擊邢杲，以北海王顥方入寇，集文武議之，眾皆曰：「杲眾強盛，宜以為先。

translations.literal: Yuan Tianmu of Wei was about to strike Xing Luo when the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, was invading; he gathered civil and military officials to deliberate, and all said: "Luo's host is strong and should be dealt with first."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu of Wei was preparing to attack Xing Luo when word came that the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, was raiding the borders; he convened civil and military officers for counsel, and all said, "Luo's forces are strong—we should strike him first."

sentences.zh: 」行台尚書薛琡曰：「邢杲兵眾雖多，鼠竊狗偷，非有遠志。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the mobile staff, Xue Zan, said: "Though Xing Luo's troops are many, they are rats stealing and dogs snatching, without far-reaching aims.
translations.idiomatic: The mobile-staff Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Xue Zan, said, "Xing Luo may field many men, but they are mere thieves and scavengers without distant ambition.

sentences.zh: 顥帝室近親，來稱義舉，其勢難測，宜先去之。

translations.literal: Hao is close kin of the imperial house and has come proclaiming a righteous rising; his momentum is hard to gauge—we should eliminate him first."
translations.idiomatic: Hao is close imperial kin and marches under the banner of a righteous cause; his momentum is hard to read—we should deal with him first."

sentences.zh: 」天穆以諸將多欲擊杲，又魏朝亦以顥為孤弱，不足慮，命天穆等先定齊地，還師擊顥，遂引兵東出。

translations.literal: Tianmu, because most generals wished to strike Luo and the Wei court also regarded Hao as isolated and not worth worry, ordered Tianmu and the others first to settle Qi territory and then return to attack Hao; he led his army east.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu, since most commanders wanted to hit Luo and the Wei court likewise judged Hao isolated and negligible, ordered his forces first to pacify Qi and only then turn on Hao; he marched east.

sentences.zh: 顥與陳慶之乘虛自銍城進拔滎城，遂至梁國；

translations.literal: Hao, with Chen Qingzhi, seized the opening from Zhi city, took Ying city, and reached the Liang region;
translations.idiomatic: Hao, with Chen Qingzhi exploiting the gap, advanced from Zhi city, captured Ying city, and pressed into the Liang region;

sentences.zh: 魏丘大千有眾七萬，分築九城以拒之。

translations.literal: Qiu Daqian of Wei had seventy thousand men and built nine walled camps to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Daqian of Wei had seventy thousand men and threw up nine walled camps to block them.

sentences.zh: 慶之攻之，自旦至申，拔其三壘，大千請降。

translations.literal: Qingzhi attacked from dawn to mid-afternoon, took three of the camps, and Daqian asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi assaulted them from dawn until mid-afternoon, seized three camps, and Daqian sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 顥登壇燔燎，即帝位於睢陽城南，改元孝基。

translations.literal: Hao ascended the altar, lit the signal fires, and took the throne south of Suiyang city, changing the era name to Xiaoji.
translations.idiomatic: Hao mounted the altar, kindled the beacon fires, and declared himself emperor south of Suiyang, taking the era name Xiaoji.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王暉業帥羽林兵二萬軍考城，慶之攻拔其城，擒暉業。

translations.literal: Prince Ye of Jiyin led twenty thousand armored guards at Kao city; Qingzhi stormed the city, captured it, and seized Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ye of Jiyin led twenty thousand armored guards at Kao city; Qingzhi stormed the place, took the city, and captured Ye.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，魏上黨王天穆及爾朱兆破邢杲於濟南，杲降，送洛陽，斬之。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and Erzhu Zhao of Wei defeated Xing Luo at Ji'nan; Luo surrendered, was sent to Luoyang, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Wei Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and Erzhu Zhao routed Xing Luo at Ji'nan; Luo surrendered, was sent to Luoyang, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 兆，榮之從子也。

translations.literal: Zhao was a nephew of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was a nephew of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳，魏以東南道大都督楊昱鎮滎陽，尚書僕射爾朱世隆鎮虎牢，侍中爾朱世承鎮崿□。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on day dingsi, Wei appointed the Grand Commander of the Southeast Circuit, Yang Yu, to garrison Yingyang, the Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Erzhu Shilong to garrison Hulao, and the Palace Attendant Erzhu Shicheng to garrison the Yao pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingsi, Wei posted the grand commander of the southeast circuit, Yang Yu, at Yingyang; the Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Erzhu Shilong, at Hulao; and the palace attendant Erzhu Shicheng at the Yao pass.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On day yichou, the court and countryside were placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, court and countryside were placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，北海王顥克梁國。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, took the Liang region.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, captured the Liang region.

sentences.zh: 顥以陳慶之為衛將軍，徐州刺史，引兵而西。

translations.literal: Hao made Chen Qingzhi Defender-General and regional inspector of Xuzhou and led his army west.
translations.idiomatic: Hao appointed Chen Qingzhi Defender-General and inspector of Xuzhou and marched west.

sentences.zh: 楊昱擁眾七萬，據滎陽。

translations.literal: Yang Yu held seventy thousand men and occupied Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu held seventy thousand men and fortified Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 慶之攻之，未拔。

translations.literal: Qingzhi attacked but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi besieged the city but could not break it.

sentences.zh: 顥遣人說昱使降，昱不從。

translations.literal: Hao sent men to persuade Yu to surrender; Yu would not.
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent envoys to urge Yu to surrender; Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 元天穆與驃騎將軍爾朱吐沒兒將大軍前後繼至，梁士卒皆恐。

translations.literal: Yuan Tianmu and the General of Agile Cavalry Erzhu Tumener led great armies arriving in succession, and the Liang soldiers were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu and the General of Agile Cavalry, Erzhu Tumener, brought up great armies one after another, and the Liang troops were seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 慶之解鞍秣馬，諭將士曰：「吾至此以來，屠城略地，實為不少；

translations.literal: Qingzhi unslung his saddle and fed his horse, then addressed the officers and men: "Since I came here I have stormed cities and overrun territory—indeed, quite a lot;
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi loosed his saddle, fed his horse, and addressed officers and men: "Since we crossed the river we have stormed cities and overrun lands—no small tally;

sentences.zh: 君等殺人父兄、掠人子女，亦無算矣。

translations.literal: you have killed others' fathers and elder brothers and seized others' sons and daughters beyond counting as well.
translations.idiomatic: you have killed fathers and elder brothers and seized sons and daughters beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 天穆之眾，皆是仇讎。

translations.literal: Tianmu's host are all our enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu's men are every one our enemies.

sentences.zh: 我輩眾才七千，虜眾三十餘萬，今日之事，唯有必死乃可得生耳！

translations.literal: We number only seven thousand, while the foe has more than three hundred thousand; today's affair can end only in certain death if we are to live!"
translations.idiomatic: We are barely seven thousand; the enemy fields more than three hundred thousand. Today we live only if we stake everything on death!"

sentences.zh: 虜騎多，不可與之野戰，當及其未盡至，急攻取其城而據之。

translations.literal: The enemy cavalry are many; we cannot meet them in open field. We must strike before they are all here, press the attack, take the city, and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Their cavalry are too many for open battle. Before the rest arrive, we must storm the city and hold it.

sentences.zh: 諸君勿或狐疑，自取屠膾！

translations.literal: Do not waver in doubt and bring slaughter on yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not falter in doubt and make yourselves butcher's meat!"

sentences.zh: 」乃鼓之，使登城。

translations.literal: He then beat the drums and ordered them up the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the drums and ordered them onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 將士即相帥蟻附而入，癸酉，拔滎陽，執楊昱。

translations.literal: Officers and men at once climbed in swarms like ants; on day guiyou they took Yingyang and seized Yang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men swarmed up like ants; on guiyou they stormed Yingyang and captured Yang Yu.

sentences.zh: 諸將三百餘人伏顥帳前請曰：「陛下渡江三千里，無遺鏃之費，昨滎陽城下一朝殺傷五百餘人，願乞楊昱以快眾意！

translations.literal: More than three hundred generals knelt before Hao's tent and pleaded: "Your Majesty has crossed the river three thousand li without losing an arrow; yet below Yingyang city in one morning more than five hundred were killed and wounded—we beg Yang Yu to satisfy the host!"
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred commanders knelt before Hao's tent and said, "Your Majesty marched three thousand li without wasting a shaft; yet below Yingyang we lost over five hundred in a single morning—grant us Yang Yu to appease the troops!"

sentences.zh: 」顥曰：「我在江東聞梁主言，初舉兵下都，袁昂為吳郡不降，每稱其忠節。

translations.literal: Hao said: "When I was east of the river I heard the Liang ruler say that when he first raised arms and descended on the capital, Yuan Ang of Wu commandery would not submit, and he always praised Ang's loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "East of the river I heard the Liang ruler say that when he first marched on the capital, Yuan Ang of Wu commandery would not submit, and he always praised Ang's loyal steadfastness.

sentences.zh: 楊昱忠臣，奈何殺之！

translations.literal: Yang Yu is a loyal minister—how can we kill him!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu is a loyal minister—how can we kill him!

sentences.zh: 此外唯卿等所取。

translations.literal: Apart from him, take what you will."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from him, take what you will."

sentences.zh: 」於是斬昱所部統帥三十七人，皆刳心而食之。

translations.literal: Thereupon thirty-seven commanders under Yu were beheaded; all had their hearts cut out and were eaten.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon thirty-seven of Yu's commanders were beheaded; each had his heart cut out and was eaten.

sentences.zh: 俄而天穆等引兵圍城，慶之帥騎三千背城力戰，大破之，天穆、吐沒兒皆走。

translations.literal: Soon Tianmu and the others brought troops to encircle the city; Qingzhi led three thousand horsemen to fight with their backs to the wall and routed them; Tianmu and Tumener both fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tianmu and the others invested the city; Qingzhi led three thousand horsemen in a fight with their backs to the wall and smashed them; Tianmu and Tumener both fled.

sentences.zh: 慶之進擊虎牢，爾朱世隆棄城走，獲魏東中郎將辛纂。

translations.literal: Qingzhi pressed the attack on Hulao; Erzhu Shilong abandoned the city and fled, and they captured the Wei Eastern Palace Attendant Xin Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi pressed on to Hulao; Erzhu Shilong abandoned the city and fled, and they took the Wei Eastern Palace Attendant, Xin Zuan.

sentences.zh: 魏主將出避顥，未知所之，或勸之長安，中書舍人高道穆曰：「關中荒殘，何可復往！

translations.literal: The Wei ruler was about to leave to avoid Hao and did not know where to go; some urged Chang'an. The Palace Attendant Gao Daomu said: "Guanzhong is wasted and ruined—how can we go there again!
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor was about to flee before Hao and did not know where to turn; some urged Chang'an. The Palace Attendant Gao Daomu said, "Guanzhong lies in ruins—how can we go back there!

sentences.zh: 顥士眾不多，乘虛深入，由將帥不得其人，故能至此。

translations.literal: Hao's soldiers are not numerous; penetrating deeply on a gap is only because the commanders are unworthy, and that is why they have come this far.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's troops are not numerous; they have pierced this deep only because our commanders are unfit—that is why they stand here.

sentences.zh: 陛下若親帥宿衛，高募重賞，背城一戰，臣等竭其死力，破顥孤軍必矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty personally leads the palace guard, offers high rewards at great cost, and fights one battle with your back to the wall, we your servants will spend our lives, and Hao's lone army will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty personally leads the palace guard, posts lavish bounties, and fights one battle with the wall at your back, we will spend our lives to the last man and surely break Hao's isolated army.

sentences.zh: 或恐勝負難期，則車賀不若渡河，征大將軍天穆、大丞相榮各使引兵來會，犄角進討，旬月之間，必見成功。

translations.literal: Or, if victory and defeat are hard to foresee, then it is better to take carriage and guest and cross the river, summon the Grand General Tianmu and the Grand Chancellor Rong each to bring troops to join, and advance in pincers—within ten days or a month success will appear.
translations.idiomatic: If the outcome is hard to foresee, better to cross the river in state: summon the grand general Tianmu and the grand chancellor Rong, have each bring his host, and close in from two sides—in ten days or a month success will show.

sentences.zh: 此萬全之策也。

translations.literal: This is the plan of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: That is the plan without flaw."

sentences.zh: 」魏主從之。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏主北行，夜，至河內郡北，命高道穆於燭下作詔書數十紙，佈告遠近。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu the Wei ruler went north; at night he reached the north of Henei commandery and ordered Gao Daomu by candlelight to draft several dozen edicts and proclaim them far and near.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the Wei emperor marched north; that night he reached the north of Henei commandery and ordered Gao Daomu by lamplight to draft dozens of edicts and proclaim them far and wide.

sentences.zh: 於是四方始知魏主所在。

translations.literal: Only then did the four quarters learn where the Wei ruler was.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the realm learn where the Wei emperor stood.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏主入河內。

translations.literal: On day yihai the Wei ruler entered Henei.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the Wei emperor entered Henei.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧、安豐王延明，帥百僚，封府庫，備法駕迎顥。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, and Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, led the hundred officials to seal the treasuries and storehouses and prepared the imperial equipage to welcome Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, and Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, led the hundred officials to seal the treasuries and prepared the imperial equipage to welcome Hao.

sentences.zh: 丙子，顥入洛陽宮，改元建武，大赦。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Hao entered the Luoyang palace, changed the era name to Jianwu, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Hao entered the Luoyang palace, changed the era name to Jianwu, and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以陳慶之為侍中、車騎大將軍，增邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Chen Qingzhi was made Palace Attendant and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with a fief increase of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi was made palace attendant and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with his fief increased by ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 楊椿在洛陽，椿弟順為冀州刺史，兄子侃為北中郎將，從魏主在河北。

translations.literal: Yang Chun was in Luoyang; Chun's younger brother Shun was regional inspector of Ji, and his nephew Kan was Northern Palace General—all followed the Wei ruler in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun remained in Luoyang; his younger brother Shun was inspector of Ji, and his nephew Kan was Northern Palace General—all were with the Wei emperor in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 顥意忌椿，而以其家世顯重，恐失人望，未敢誅也。

translations.literal: Hao resented Chun, but because his family had long been eminent he feared losing popular regard and did not yet dare execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao resented Chun, but because the clan had long been eminent he feared losing hearts and did not yet dare kill him.

sentences.zh: 或勸椿出亡，椿曰：「吾內外百口，何所逃匿！

translations.literal: Some urged Chun to flee; Chun said: "Within and without, our household numbers a hundred mouths—where could we flee!
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Chun to flee; Chun said, "A hundred mouths in and out of this house—where would we run!

sentences.zh: 正當坐待天命耳。

translations.literal: We should simply sit and await Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: We can only sit and await Heaven's decree."

sentences.zh: 顥後軍都督侯暄守睢陽，為後援。

translations.literal: Hao's Rear Army Commander Hou Xuan garrisoned Suiyang as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's rear-army commander Hou Xuan held Suiyang as a rear base.

sentences.zh: 魏行台崔孝芬、大都督刁宣馳往圍暄，晝夜急攻，戊寅，暄突走，擒斬之。

translations.literal: The Wei mobile-staff Director Cui Xiaofen and Grand Commander Diao Xuan galloped to invest Xuan, attacking day and night; on day wuyin, Xuan broke out and fled and was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei mobile-staff director Cui Xiaofen and grand commander Diao Xuan raced to besiege Xuan, attacking day and night; on wuyin, Xuan broke out, fled, and was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 上黨王天穆等帥眾四萬攻拔大梁，分遣費穆將兵二萬攻虎牢，顥使陳慶之擊之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and others led forty thousand men, took Daliang, and detached Fei Mu with twenty thousand to attack Hulao; Hao sent Chen Qingzhi to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and others led forty thousand men, captured Daliang, and detached Fei Mu with twenty thousand to storm Hulao; Hao sent Chen Qingzhi against him.

sentences.zh: 天穆畏顥，將北渡河，謂行台郎中濟陰溫子升曰：「卿欲向洛，為隨我北渡？

translations.literal: Tianmu feared Hao and was about to cross the river north; he said to the mobile-staff gentleman Wen Zisheng of Jiyin: "Do you wish to go to Luo, or follow me north across the river?"
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu feared Hao and prepared to cross north; he asked the mobile-staff gentleman Wen Zisheng of Jiyin, "Do you mean to go to Luoyang, or follow me north across the river?"

sentences.zh: 」子升曰：「主上以虎牢失守，致此狼狽。

translations.literal: Zisheng said: "Because Your Lordship lost Hulao, things came to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng said, "Because tiger pass was lost, affairs came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 元顥新入，人情未安，今往擊之，無不克者。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao has only just entered; hearts are not yet settled—strike now and none can stand.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao has only just entered; hearts are not yet settled—strike now and none can stand.

sentences.zh: 大王平定京邑，奉迎大駕，此恆、文之舉也。

translations.literal: If Your Lordship pacifies the capital and welcomes the great equipage, this is an achievement like Huan and Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Pacify the capital and welcome the great equipage—that is an achievement like Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 捨此北渡，竊為大王惜之。

translations.literal: To abandon this and cross north—I venture it is a loss for Your Lordship."
translations.idiomatic: To cast this aside and cross north—I fear Your Lordship will regret it."

sentences.zh: 」天穆善之而不能用，遂引兵渡河。

translations.literal: Tianmu approved but could not act on it and led his army across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu approved but could not bring himself to act; he led his army across the river.

sentences.zh: 費穆攻虎牢，將拔，聞天穆北渡，自以無後繼，遂降於慶之。

translations.literal: Fei Mu attacked Hulao and was about to take it when he heard Tianmu had crossed north; thinking he had no support behind him, he surrendered to Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu assaulted Hulao and was on the verge of taking it when he heard Tianmu had crossed north; believing he had no rear, he surrendered to Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 慶之進擊大梁、梁國，皆下之。

translations.literal: Qingzhi pressed attacks on Daliang and the Liang region and took both.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi pressed Daliang and the Liang region and took both.

sentences.zh: 慶之以數千之眾，自發銍縣至洛陽，凡取三十二城，四十七戰，所向皆克。

translations.literal: With a few thousand men Qingzhi, from the time he set out from Zhi county to Luoyang, took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles; wherever he turned, he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: With only a few thousand men, from his departure at Zhi county to Luoyang, Qingzhi took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles; wherever he turned, he prevailed.

sentences.zh: 顥使黃門郎祖瑩作書遺魏主曰：「朕泣請梁朝，誓在復恥，正欲問罪於爾朱，出卿於桎梏。

translations.literal: Hao had the Yellow Gate Gentleman Zu Ying draft a letter to the Wei ruler, saying: "I wept and begged the Liang court, swearing to wipe away shame, intending only to call Erzhu to account and release you from fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had the Yellow Gate Gentleman Zu Ying draft a letter to the Wei emperor: "I wept and begged the Liang court, swearing to wipe away disgrace, meaning only to call Erzhu to account and free you from bonds.

sentences.zh: 卿托命豺狼，委身虎口，假獲民地，本是榮物，固非卿有。

translations.literal: You entrusted your life to wolves and tigers and cast your body into the tiger's maw; the people's land you seized in name was originally Rong's spoil and was never yours.
translations.idiomatic: You entrusted your life to wolves and cast your body into a tiger's maw; the people's land you hold was always Rong's prize and was never truly yours.

sentences.zh: 今國家隆替，在卿與我。

translations.literal: Now the state's rise or fall lies between you and me.
translations.idiomatic: Now whether the state rises or falls lies between you and me.

sentences.zh: 若天道助順，則皇魏再興；

translations.literal: If Heaven's Way aids the righteous, the great Wei will rise again;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven aids the righteous, great Wei will rise again;

sentences.zh: 脫或不然，在榮為福，於卿為禍。

translations.literal: if not, for Rong it is fortune, for you disaster.
translations.idiomatic: if not, fortune for Rong, disaster for you.

sentences.zh: 卿宜三復，富貴可保。

translations.literal: Consider thrice, and wealth and rank may be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Think thrice, and wealth and rank may yet be kept."

sentences.zh: 顥既入洛，自河以南州郡多附之。

translations.literal: Once Hao had entered Luo, south of the river most commanderies and prefectures submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hao held Luoyang, most prefectures and commanderies south of the river submitted.

sentences.zh: 齊州刺史沛郡王欣集文武議所從，曰：「北海、長樂，俱帝室近親，今宗祏不移，我欲受赦，諸君意何如？

translations.literal: The regional inspector of Qi, Prince Xin of Pei commandery, gathered civil and military officials to decide whom to follow, saying: "The Princes of Beihai and Changle are both close imperial kin; now the ancestral temple is not moved—I wish to accept the amnesty; what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Qi, Prince Xin of Pei commandery, gathered officers to decide whom to follow: "The princes of Beihai and Changle are both close imperial kin; the ancestral temple has not been removed—I mean to accept the amnesty; what say you?"

sentences.zh: 」在坐莫不失色。

translations.literal: Those seated all lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone present went pale.

sentences.zh: 軍司崔光韶獨抗言曰：「元顥受制於梁，引寇仇之兵以覆宗國，此魏之賊臣亂子也。

translations.literal: The army aide Cui Guangshao alone spoke against it: "Yuan Hao is controlled by Liang and leads an enemy host to overturn the ancestral state—he is Wei's traitorous minister and rebellious son.
translations.idiomatic: Only the army aide Cui Guangshao spoke against it: "Yuan Hao is Liang's puppet and leads a hostile army to overturn the ancestral state—he is Wei's traitor and rebellious son.

sentences.zh: 豈唯大王家事所宜切齒，下官等皆荷朝眷，未敢仰從！

translations.literal: This is not only a matter your Highness should gnash his teeth over—we your servants all owe the court's grace and dare not comply from below!"
translations.idiomatic: This is not only a matter for Your Highness to gnash his teeth over—we who owe the court's grace dare not obey from below!"

sentences.zh: 」長史崔景茂等皆曰：「軍司議是。

translations.literal: The chief clerk Cui Jingmao and the others all said: "The army aide is right."
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk Cui Jingmao and the others all said, "The army aide is right."

sentences.zh: 」欣乃斬顥使。

translations.literal: Xin then beheaded Hao's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Xin then beheaded Hao's envoy.

sentences.zh: 光韶，亮之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Guangshao was a younger cousin of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshao was a younger cousin of Cui Liang.

sentences.zh: 於是襄州刺史賈思同、廣州刺史鄭先護、南兗州刺史元暹亦不受顥命。

translations.literal: Thereupon the regional inspector of Xiang, Jia Sitong, the regional inspector of Guang, Zheng Xianhu, and the regional inspector of Southern Yan, Yuan Xian, also refused Hao's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the inspector of Xiang, Jia Sitong; of Guang, Zheng Xianhu; and of Southern Yan, Yuan Xian, likewise refused Hao's orders.

sentences.zh: 思同，思伯之弟也。

translations.literal: Sitong was the younger brother of Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong was the younger brother of Sibo.

sentences.zh: 顥以冀州刺史元孚為東道行台、彭城郡王，孚封送其書於魏主。

translations.literal: Hao made Yuan Fu, regional inspector of Ji, Eastern Circuit mobile-staff director and Prince of Pengcheng commandery; Fu sealed and forwarded his letter to the Wei ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Hao appointed Yuan Fu, inspector of Ji, as eastern-circuit mobile-staff director and Prince of Pengcheng; Fu sealed Hao's letter and forwarded it to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 平陽王敬先起兵於河橋以討顥，不克而死。

translations.literal: Prince Jingxian of Pingyang, Jingxian, raised troops at He Bridge to attack Hao, failed, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingxian of Pingyang raised troops at He Bridge to attack Hao, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 魏以侍中、車騎將軍、尚書右僕射爾朱世隆為使持節、行台僕射、大將軍、相州刺史，鎮鄴城。

translations.literal: Wei made the Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Erzhu Shilong Bearer of the Staff, Acting Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the mobile staff, Grand General, and regional inspector of Xiang, to garrison Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Erzhu Shilong bearer of the staff, acting mobile-staff vice director, grand general, and inspector of Xiang, to hold Ye city.

sentences.zh: 魏主之出也，單騎而去，侍衛後宮皆案堵如故。

translations.literal: When the Wei ruler departed, he went off with a single horse; the palace guard and inner quarters all remained undisturbed as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor fled, he rode off alone; the palace guard and inner quarters remained undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 顥一旦得之，號令己出，四方人情想其風政。

translations.literal: Once Hao had it in a day, his orders issued forth, and popular sentiment everywhere looked to his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hao held power, his orders went forth and people everywhere looked to his rule.

sentences.zh: 而顥自謂天授，遽有驕怠之志。

translations.literal: But Hao, thinking Heaven had granted it to him, abruptly took on an arrogant, negligent will.
translations.idiomatic: But Hao, believing Heaven had handed him the throne, soon grew arrogant and careless.

sentences.zh: 宿昔賓客近習，鹹見寵待，干擾政事，日夜縱酒，不恤軍國，所從南兵，陵暴市裡，朝野失望。

translations.literal: His old guests and close attendants were all favored and pampered, meddling in government affairs; he drank day and night without caring for army or state; the southern troops who followed him bullied the markets—court and countryside lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: Old clients and close attendants were showered with favor and meddled in government; he drank day and night and neglected army and state; the southern soldiers who followed him bullied the markets, and court and countryside lost heart.

sentences.zh: 高道穆兄子儒自洛陽出從魏主，魏主問洛中事，子儒曰：「顥敗在旦夕，不足憂也。

translations.literal: Gao Daomu's nephew Ru came out from Luoyang to join the Wei ruler; the Wei ruler asked about affairs in Luo, and Ru said: "Hao's defeat is a matter of days—nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daomu's nephew Ru left Luoyang to join the Wei emperor; asked about Luo, Ru said, "Hao will fall within days—there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」爾朱榮聞魏主北出，即時馳傳見魏主於長子，行，且部分。

translations.literal: " Erzhu Rong, hearing the Wei ruler had gone north, at once galloped by post to see the Wei ruler at Changzi, marching and deploying as he went.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, hearing the emperor had fled north, galloped by post to meet him at Changzi, marching and deploying as he went.

sentences.zh: 魏主即日南還，榮為前驅。

translations.literal: That same day the Wei ruler turned south; Rong served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Wei emperor turned south, with Rong in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，兵眾大集，資糧器仗，相繼而至。

translations.literal: Within ten days or so, troops massed in great numbers, and provisions, grain, and weapons arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days hosts massed, and grain, supplies, and arms arrived in steady streams.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬午，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day renwu, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renwu, Wei proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 榮既南下，並、肆不安，乃以爾朱天光為並、肆等九州行台，仍行并州事。

translations.literal: Once Rong had marched south, Bing and Xi were unsettled; he therefore made Erzhu Tianguang mobile-staff director for nine provinces including Bing and Xi, while still conducting affairs of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong marched south, Bing and Xi grew restless; he made Erzhu Tianguang mobile-staff director over nine provinces including Bing and Xi while still governing Bing.

sentences.zh: 天光至晉陽，部分約勒，所部皆安。

translations.literal: Tianguang reached Jinyang, deployed and restrained his command, and all under him were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tianguang reached Jinyang, organized and disciplined his command, and all under him were pacified.

sentences.zh: 己丑，費穆至洛陽，顥引入，責以河陰之事而殺之。

translations.literal: On day jichou, Fei Mu reached Luoyang; Hao brought him in, blamed him for the affair at Heyin, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Fei Mu reached Luoyang; Hao received him, blamed him for the massacre at Heyin, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 顥使都督宗正珍孫與河內太守元襲據河內；

translations.literal: Hao sent the commander Zongzheng Zhensun and the Administrator of Henei, Yuan Xi, to hold Henei;
translations.idiomatic: Hao sent the commander Zongzheng Zhensun and the administrator of Henei, Yuan Xi, to hold Henei;

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮攻之，上黨王天穆引兵會之，壬寅，拔其城，斬珍孫及襲。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong attacked them; the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, led troops to join him; on day renyin they took the city and beheaded Zhensun and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong attacked them; the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, joined him; on renyin they stormed the city and beheaded Zhensun and Xi.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，魏淮陰太守晉鴻以湖陽來降。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, Jin Hong, Administrator of Huaiyin in Wei, surrendered Huyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Jin Hong, Wei administrator of Huaiyin, surrendered Huyang.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己未，南康簡王績卒。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on day jiwei, Prince Jian of Nankang, Ji, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jiwei, Prince Jian of Nankang, Ji, died.

sentences.zh: 魏北海王顥既得志，密與臨淮王彧、安豐王延明謀叛梁；

translations.literal: Once the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, had achieved his aim, he secretly plotted rebellion against Liang with Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, and Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming;
translations.idiomatic: Once the Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, had achieved his aim, he secretly plotted to turn against Liang with Princes Huai of Linhuai and Anfeng, Yuan Yu and Yuan Yanming;

sentences.zh: 以事難未平，藉陳慶之兵力，故外同內異，言多猜忌。

translations.literal: because affairs were not yet settled, he relied on Chen Qingzhi's military strength; outwardly they agreed, inwardly they differed, and their words were full of suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: because the realm was not yet settled he still needed Chen Qingzhi's troops; outwardly they agreed, inwardly they doubted one another.

sentences.zh: 慶之亦密為之備，說顥曰：「今遠來至此，未服者尚多，彼若知吾虛實，連兵四合，將何以御之！

translations.literal: Qingzhi also secretly made preparations and said to Hao: "Having come far to this place, many are still unsubmissive; if they learn our true strength and link armies on four sides, how will we defend against them!
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi also quietly prepared and told Hao, "We have marched far, and many here are still unsubmissive; if they learn how few we are and link armies on every side, how will we hold them off?

sentences.zh: 宜啟天子，更請精兵，並敕諸州，有南人沒此者悉須部送。

translations.literal: You should inform the Son of Heaven and request more picked troops, and also order the provinces that any southerners captured here must all be sent under command."
translations.idiomatic: You should inform the Son of Heaven and ask for more picked troops, and order every province to send here all southerners it holds under arms."

sentences.zh: 」顥欲從之，延明曰：「慶之兵不出數千，已自難制；

translations.literal: Hao wished to follow this; Yanming said: "Qingzhi's troops number only a few thousand and are already hard to control;
translations.idiomatic: Hao meant to agree; Yanming said, "Qingzhi commands only a few thousand men and is already hard to control;

sentences.zh: 今更增其眾，寧肯復為人用乎！

translations.literal: if you now increase his host, will he consent to be used by others again!
translations.idiomatic: if you swell his host now, will he still let others command him?

sentences.zh: 大權一去，動息由人，魏之宗廟，於斯墜矣。

translations.literal: Once great power is gone, every move depends on others—the ancestral temple of Wei will fall at this stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Once great power passes from your hands, every move depends on others—the Wei ancestral temple will topple with it.

sentences.zh: 」顥乃不用慶之言。

translations.literal: " Hao therefore did not adopt Qingzhi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Hao therefore ignored Qingzhi's advice.

sentences.zh: 又慮慶之密啟，乃表於上曰：「今河北、河南一時克定，唯爾朱榮尚敢跋扈，臣與慶之自能擒討。

translations.literal: He also feared Qingzhi would secretly report him, and therefore memorialized the throne: "Now Hebei and Henan are for the moment pacified; only Erzhu Rong still dares to be overbearing—your servant and Qingzhi can capture and punish him ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Qingzhi might report him in secret, he memorialized the throne: "Hebei and Henan are for the moment pacified; only Erzhu Rong still dares to swagger—your servant and Qingzhi can seize him ourselves.

sentences.zh: 州郡新服，正須綏撫，不宜更復加兵，搖動百姓。

translations.literal: The provinces and commanderies have newly submitted and need soothing governance; we should not add more troops and shake the people."
translations.idiomatic: The provinces have only just submitted and need soothing rule; we must not add more troops and unsettle the people."

sentences.zh: 」上乃詔諸軍繼進者皆停於境上。

translations.literal: " The Emperor therefore ordered all armies that were to follow up to halt at the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor therefore ordered every army meant to follow up to halt at the borders.

sentences.zh: 洛中南兵不滿一萬，而羌、胡之眾十倍，軍副馬佛念為慶之曰：「將軍威行河、洛，聲震中原，功高勢重，為魏所疑，一旦變生不測，可無慮乎！

translations.literal: The southern troops in Luo numbered fewer than ten thousand, while the Qiang and Hu were ten times as many; the army aide Ma Fonian spoke for Qingzhi: "General, your prestige runs through He and Luo and your name shakes the central plain; your merit is high and your power heavy—the Wei court will suspect you; once unforeseen change arises, can you be without worry!
translations.idiomatic: Southern troops in Luoyang numbered fewer than ten thousand, while Qiang and Hu levies were ten times as many; the army aide Ma Fonian urged Qingzhi: "General, your fame fills the Yellow River lands and your merit outweighs your rank—the Wei court must suspect you; if fortune turns, will you not be in peril?

sentences.zh: 不若乘其無備，殺顥據洛，此千載一時也。

translations.literal: Why not seize their unpreparedness, kill Hao, and hold Luo—this is a chance of a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Strike while they are unready, kill Hao, and hold Luoyang—such a chance comes once in a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 」慶之不從。

translations.literal: Qingzhi would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi refused.

sentences.zh: 顥先以慶之為徐州刺史，因固求之鎮，顥心憚之，不遣，曰：「主上以洛陽之地全相任委，忽聞捨此朝寄，欲往彭城，謂君遽取富貴，不為國計，非徒有損於君，恐僕並受其責。

translations.literal: Hao had earlier made Qingzhi regional inspector of Xuzhou; because he firmly asked to garrison there, Hao feared him in his heart and would not send him, saying: "The sovereign above has wholly entrusted you with the Luoyang region; suddenly to hear you would abandon this court commission and go to Pengcheng—people will think you are hastening after wealth and not planning for the state; this harms not only you but I fear we shall both be blamed."
translations.idiomatic: Hao had earlier made Qingzhi inspector of Xuzhou; when Qingzhi pressed to take up that post, Hao feared him and refused, saying, "The throne has wholly entrusted Luoyang to you; to abandon that charge for Pengcheng will look like grasping for wealth, not serving the state—you harm yourself, and I fear we shall both be blamed."

sentences.zh: 」慶之不敢復言。

translations.literal: Qingzhi dared not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi dared not raise it again.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮與顥相持於河上。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong and Hao faced each other along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong and Hao faced each other along the river.

sentences.zh: 慶之守北中城，顥自據南岸；

translations.literal: Qingzhi held North Central Fort; Hao himself held the south bank;
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi held North Central Fort while Hao held the south bank;

sentences.zh: 慶之三日十一戰，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: in three days Qingzhi fought eleven battles, with many killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: in three days Qingzhi fought eleven battles, with heavy casualties on both sides.

sentences.zh: 有夏州義士為顥守河中渚，陰與榮通謀，求破橋立效，榮引兵赴之。

translations.literal: A righteous man of Xia province held an islet in mid-river for Hao, secretly communicated with Rong, and asked to break the bridge and show merit; Rong led troops to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: A loyalist from Xia province held a mid-river islet for Hao, secretly treated with Rong, and offered to break the bridge; Rong marched to support him.

sentences.zh: 及橋破，榮應接不逮，顥悉屠之，榮悵然失望。

translations.literal: When the bridge was broken, Rong could not come up in time; Hao slaughtered them all, and Rong was deeply disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: When the bridge fell, Rong could not arrive in time; Hao slaughtered the loyalists, and Rong was bitterly disappointed.

sentences.zh: 又以安豐王延明緣河固守，而北軍無船可渡，議欲還北，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Moreover Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, held the line along the river, while the northern army had no boats to cross; they discussed returning north and planning again later.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anfeng Yanming held the river line, and the northern army had no boats; they debated retreating north to try again later.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎楊侃曰：「大王發并州之日，已知夏州義士之謀指來應之邪？

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Yang Kan said: "When the Great King set out from Bing province, did you already know the Xia loyalists' plan was to come answer you?
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Gate Gentleman Yang Kan said, "When you marched from Bing province, did you already know the Xia loyalists meant to answer you?

sentences.zh: 為欲廣施經略匡復帝室乎？

translations.literal: Or did you mean broadly to deploy strategy and restore the imperial house?
translations.idiomatic: Or did you mean to deploy your hosts and restore the imperial house?

sentences.zh: 夫用兵者，何嘗不散而更合，瘡愈更戰；

translations.literal: In warfare, has there ever been an army that did not scatter and reunite, or a wound that healed and then fought again;
translations.idiomatic: In war, armies scatter and gather again, wounds heal and men fight again;

sentences.zh: 況今未有所損，豈可以一事不諧而眾謀頓廢乎！

translations.literal: moreover we have not yet suffered loss—how can one setback make you abandon the whole plan!
translations.idiomatic: and we have not yet suffered real loss—how can one setback scrap the whole design?

sentences.zh: 今四方顒顒，視公此舉；

translations.literal: Now the four quarters watch eagerly what you do;
translations.idiomatic: Now the four quarters watch eagerly what you will do;

sentences.zh: 若未有所成，遽復引歸，民情失望，各懷去就，勝負所在，未可知也。

translations.literal: if you achieve nothing and hastily withdraw, popular hearts will lose hope, each will think of leaving, and where victory lies is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: if you achieve nothing and pull back, hearts will fail, men will think of leaving, and victory is anyone's guess.

sentences.zh: 不若征發民材，多為桴筏，間以舟楫，緣河布列，數百里中，皆為渡勢，首尾既遠，使顥不知所防，一旦得渡，必立大功。

translations.literal: Better to levy civilian timber, make many rafts, add boats here and there, array along the river for hundreds of li, all as crossing positions; with head and tail far apart, Hao will not know where to guard—once we cross in a day, great merit is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Better to levy timber, build rafts and boats, and array crossings for hundreds of li—head and tail far apart so Hao cannot guess where we will strike; cross once, and merit is certain."

sentences.zh: 」高道穆曰：「今乘輿飄蕩，主憂臣辱。

translations.literal: Gao Daomu said: "Now the imperial carriage drifts in peril—the ruler grieves and ministers are shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daomu said, "The imperial carriage drifts in peril—the ruler grieves and ministers are shamed.

sentences.zh: 大王擁百萬之眾，輔天子而令諸侯，若分兵造筏，所在散渡，指掌可克；

translations.literal: Great King, you hold a host of a million, assisting the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords—if you divide troops to build rafts and cross here and there, it can be taken in a gesture;
translations.idiomatic: You command a million men, assisting the Son of Heaven to command the lords—divide troops, build rafts, and cross piecemeal, and victory is at hand;

sentences.zh: 奈何捨之北歸，使顥復得完聚，徵兵天下！

translations.literal: why abandon this and return north, letting Hao gather his strength again and levy troops throughout the realm!
translations.idiomatic: why turn north and let Hao gather strength and levy the realm again!

sentences.zh: 此所謂養虺成蛇，悔無及矣。

translations.literal: This is what they call nurturing a viper to your sorrow, with regret too late."
translations.idiomatic: That is to nurture a viper you will regret forever."

sentences.zh: 」榮曰：「楊黃門已陳此策，當相與議之。

translations.literal: Rong said: "Yellow Gate Yang has already set forth this plan; we should deliberate it together."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Yellow Gate Yang has already offered this plan; we shall discuss it together."

sentences.zh: 」劉靈助言於榮曰：「不出十日，河南必平。

translations.literal: Liu Lingzhu said to Rong: "Within ten days Henan will surely be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingzhu told Rong, "Within ten days Henan will be pacified."

sentences.zh: 」伏波將軍正平楊心剽與其族居馬渚，自言有小船數艘，求為鄉導。

translations.literal: The General Who Subdues Waves, Yang Xin the Corrector of Ping, lived with his clan at Ma islet and said he had several small boats, asking to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Subdues Waves, Yang Xin the Corrector of Ping, lived with his clan at Horse Ford and offered several small boats as guide.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，榮命車騎將軍爾朱兆與大都督賀拔勝縛材為筏，自馬渚西硤石夜渡，襲擊顥子領軍將軍冠受，擒之；

translations.literal: On day wuchen, Rong ordered the Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Erzhu Zhao and the Grand Commander Heba Sheng to bind timber as rafts; from Ma Ford they crossed west at Xiashi by night, struck Hao's son and commander-in-chief Guan Shou, and captured him;
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Rong ordered Erzhu Zhao and the grand commander Heba Sheng to bind rafts; from Horse Ford they crossed by night at Xiashi, struck Hao's son and commander-in-chief Guan Shou, and captured him;

sentences.zh: 安豐王延明之眾聞之，大潰。

translations.literal: when the host of Prince of Anfeng, Yanming, heard this, it collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: when Prince of Anfeng Yanming's host heard this, it broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 顥失據，帥麾下數百騎南走，陳慶之收步騎數千，結陳東還，顥所得諸城，一時復降於魏。

translations.literal: Hao lost his footing, led several hundred horsemen south in flight; Chen Qingzhi gathered several thousand foot and horse, formed battle lines, and marched east; the cities Hao had taken all at once submitted again to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Hao lost his footing and fled south with a few hundred horsemen; Qingzhi gathered several thousand foot and horse, formed ranks, and marched east; the cities Hao had taken at once submitted again to Wei.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮自追陳慶之，會嵩高水漲，慶之軍士死散略盡，乃削鬚髮為沙門，間行出汝陰，還建康，猶以功除右衛將軍，封永興縣侯。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong himself pursued Chen Qingzhi; the Songgao River rose in flood, and Qingzhi's soldiers died or scattered until almost none remained; he shaved his beard and hair to become a monk, slipped out by hidden paths through Ruyin, returned to Jiankang, and was still made Defender-General of the Right and Marquis of Yongxing county for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong himself pursued Qingzhi; the Songgao River flooded, and Qingzhi's men died or scattered almost to the last; he shaved his head as a monk, slipped out through Ruyin, returned to Jiankang, and was still made Defender-General of the Right and Marquis of Yongxing for his merit.

sentences.zh: 中軍大都督兼領軍大將軍楊津入宿殿中，掃灑宮庭，封閉府庫，出迎魏主於北邙，流涕謝罪，帝慰勞之。

translations.literal: The Grand Commander of the Central Army and concurrent Defender-General Yang Jin entered to lodge in the palace hall, swept the palace courts, sealed the treasuries and storehouses, went out to welcome the Wei ruler at Northern Mang, wept and apologized for his fault; the Emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander of the Central Army and concurrent Defender-General Yang Jin lodged in the palace, swept the courts, sealed the treasuries, went out to welcome the Wei emperor at Northern Mang, wept, and apologized; the emperor comforted him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝入居華林園，大赦。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, the Emperor entered and dwelt in the Hualin Garden and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the emperor entered the Hualin Garden and proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以爾朱兆為車騎大將軍、儀同三司，北來軍士及隨賀文武諸立義者加五級，河北報事之官及河南立義者加二級。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Bearer of the Three Similitudes; northern soldiers and all civil and military who had joined the righteous cause received five grades of promotion; officials who reported from Hebei and those who rose in Henan received two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and bearer of the Three Similitudes; northern soldiers and all who had joined the righteous rising gained five ranks; reporters from Hebei and risers in Henan gained two.

sentences.zh: 壬申，加大丞相榮天柱大將軍，增封通前二十萬戶。

translations.literal: On day renshen, the Grand Chancellor Rong was further ennobled as Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar, with fief increased by two hundred thousand households including previous grants.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Grand Chancellor Rong was further made Grand General of the Heavenly Pillar, his fief increased by two hundred thousand households counting prior grants.

sentences.zh: 北海王顥自轘轅南出至臨穎，從騎分散，臨穎縣卒江豐斬之；

translations.literal: The Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, went south from Huanyuan to Linying; his mounted followers scattered; a soldier of Linying county, Jiang Feng, beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, fled south from Huanyuan to Linying; his escort scattered, and a Linying county soldier, Jiang Feng, beheaded him;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，傅首洛陽。

translations.literal: on day guiyou, the head was sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: on guiyou, the head was sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧復自歸於魏主，安豐王延明攜妻子來奔。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, again returned himself to the Wei ruler; Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, came fleeing with wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Linhuai, Yuan Yu, submitted again to the Wei emperor; Prince of Anfeng, Yuan Yanming, fled in with wife and children.

sentences.zh: 陳慶之之入洛也，蕭贊送啟求還。

translations.literal: When Chen Qingzhi entered Luo, Xiao Zan sent a memorial asking to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Qingzhi entered Luoyang, Xiao Zan sent a memorial asking to return.

sentences.zh: 時吳淑媛尚在，上使以贊幼時衣寄之，信未達而慶之敗。

translations.literal: At that time Consort Wu Shuyuan was still alive; the Emperor had her send clothes Zan had worn as a child; the letter had not arrived when Qingzhi was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu Shuyuan was still alive; the emperor had her send clothes Zan had worn as a child, but the letter had not arrived when Qingzhi fell.

sentences.zh: 慶之自魏還，特重北人，朱異怪而問之，慶之曰：「吾始以為大江以北皆戎狄之鄉，比至洛陽，乃知衣冠人物盡在中原，非江東所及也，奈何輕之？

translations.literal: When Qingzhi returned from Wei, he especially valued northerners; Zhu Yi wondered and asked him; Qingzhi said: "I once thought all north of the Great River was the land of barbarians; when I reached Luoyang, I knew that caps and gowns and cultured men were all in the central plain—not something the southeast can match—how can you slight them?
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Wei, Qingzhi especially respected northerners; Zhu Yi asked why; Qingzhi said, "I once thought everything north of the river was barbarian country; at Luoyang I learned that ritual and learning dwell in the central plain—how can the southeast slight them?

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏以上黨王天穆為太宰，城陽王徽為大司馬兼太尉。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, Wei made the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, Grand Preceptor, and the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Grand Marshal concurrent Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wei made the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, Grand Preceptor, and the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Grand Marshal and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏主宴勞爾朱榮、上黨王天穆及北來督將於都亭，出宮人三百，繒錦雜彩數萬匹，班賜有差，凡受元顥爵賞階復者，悉追奪之。

translations.literal: On day yihai, the Wei ruler feasted and rewarded Erzhu Rong, the Prince of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, and the northern commanders at the Capital Pavilion; three hundred palace women came forth, and tens of thousands of rolls of silk and brocade of mixed colors were distributed in graded gifts; all who had received ranks, rewards, and promotions from Yuan Hao had them seized back.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, the Wei emperor feasted Erzhu Rong, Yuan Tianmu, and the northern commanders at the Capital Pavilion; three hundred palace women attended, and tens of thousands of rolls of silk were given in graded gifts; everyone who had taken rank or reward from Yuan Hao had it stripped away.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛巳，魏主始入宮。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on day xinsi, the Wei ruler at last entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinsi, the Wei emperor at last entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 以高道穆為御史中尉。

translations.literal: Gao Daomu was made Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daomu was made Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 帝姊壽陽公主行犯清路，赤棒卒呵之，不止，道穆令卒擊破其車。

translations.literal: The Emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Shouyang, violated the cleared road; a red-club soldier shouted at her but she would not stop; Daomu ordered the soldier to smash her carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Shouyang, blocked the cleared road; a red-club soldier shouted at her, but she would not stop; Daomu ordered the soldier to smash her carriage.

sentences.zh: 公主泣訴於帝，帝曰：「高中尉清直之士，彼所行者公事，豈可以私責之也！

translations.literal: The princess wept and complained to the Emperor; the Emperor said: "Director Gao is an upright man; what he did was public business—how can you blame him for private reasons!
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept to the emperor; he said, "Director Gao is upright; he acted on public business—how can you blame him privately?

sentences.zh: 」道穆見帝，帝曰：「家姊行路相犯，極以為愧。

translations.literal: When Daomu saw the Emperor, the Emperor said: "My elder sister violated the road—I am deeply ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: When Daomu saw the emperor, the emperor said, "My sister blocked the road—I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 」道穆免冠謝，帝曰：「朕以愧卿，卿何謝也！

translations.literal: Daomu removed his cap and apologized; the Emperor said: "I am ashamed before you—why do you apologize!
translations.idiomatic: Daomu removed his cap and apologized; the emperor said, "I am the one ashamed—why do you apologize?

sentences.zh: 於是魏多細錢，米斗幾直一千，高道穆上表，以為：「在市銅價，八十一錢得銅一斤，私造薄錢，斤贏二百。

translations.literal: At this time Wei had much inferior coin; rice was nearly a thousand cash per dou; Gao Daomu memorialized, thinking: "At market price for copper, eighty-one cash buys one jin of copper; private minting of thin coin yields two hundred cash profit per jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei coin had grown debased; rice cost nearly a thousand cash per dou; Gao Daomu memorialized: "At market rates, eighty-one cash buys one jin of copper; private thin coin yields two hundred cash profit per jin.

sentences.zh: 既示之以深利，又隨之以重刑，抵罪雖多，奸鑄彌眾。

translations.literal: Having shown them deep profit and followed it with heavy punishment, though convictions are many, illicit casting grows ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Show deep profit, add heavy punishment, and though convictions multiply, illicit casting only spreads.

sentences.zh: 今錢徒有五銖之文，而無二銖之實，置之水上，殆欲不沉。

translations.literal: Now the coins bear the inscription of five zhu but lack two zhu in actual weight; set them on water and they nearly will not sink.
translations.idiomatic: Coins bear the five-zhu mark but lack two zhu in weight; set them on water and they barely sink.

sentences.zh: 此乃因循有漸，科防不切，朝廷失之，彼復何罪！

translations.literal: This is gradual indulgence and lax enforcement; the court has failed—what crime is theirs!
translations.idiomatic: This comes of gradual indulgence and lax enforcement—the court has failed, not the people.

sentences.zh: 宜改鑄大錢，文載年號，以記其始，則一斤所成止七十錢，計私鑄所不能自潤，直置無利，自應息心，況復嚴刑廣設也！

translations.literal: We should recast large coins, inscribe the era name in the legend to mark the beginning; then one jin would yield only seventy cash in coin—calculating, private casting could not profit itself; placed without profit, hearts should naturally rest; how much more with stern punishment broadly set!"
translations.idiomatic: Recast larger coins bearing the era name; one jin would yield only seventy cash, so private casting could not profit; without profit, the impulse dies—how much more with stern law!"

sentences.zh: 」金紫光祿大夫楊侃亦奏乞聽民與官並鑄五銖錢，使民樂為而弊自改。

translations.literal: The Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Yang Kan, also memorialized asking to let the people mint five-zhu coin together with the government so the people would gladly do it and the abuse would reform of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan also memorialized to let people mint five-zhu coin alongside the state so they would comply willingly and abuse would cure itself.

sentences.zh: 魏主從之，始鑄永安五銖錢。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler followed this and began casting Yong'an five-zhu coin.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor agreed and began casting Yong'an five-zhu coin.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，魏以車騎將軍楊津為司空。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, Wei made the Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Wei made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Jin Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，魏以梁、益二州境土荒遠，更立巴州以統諸獠，凡二十餘萬戶，以巴酋嚴始欣為刺史。

translations.literal: Initially, because the territory of Liang and Yi provinces was remote and waste, Wei established Ba province to govern the various Liao, more than two hundred thousand households, making the Ba chieftain Yan Shixin regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang and Yi were remote, Wei had established Ba province to govern the Liao peoples—more than two hundred thousand households—and made the Ba chieftain Yan Shixin inspector.

sentences.zh: 又立隆城鎮，以始欣族子愷為鎮將。

translations.literal: They also established Longcheng garrison, making Shixin's clansman Kai garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: They also established Longcheng garrison and made Shixin's kinsman Kai garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 始欣貪暴，孝昌初，諸獠反，圍州城，行台魏子建撫諭之，乃散。

translations.literal: Shixin was greedy and violent; at the start of Xiaochang, the various Liao rebelled, besieged the provincial city; the mobile-staff director Wei Zijian soothed them, and they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin was greedy and brutal; early in Xiaochang the Liao rebelled and besieged the provincial seat; mobile-staff director Wei Zijian soothed them and they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 始欣恐獲罪，陰來請降，帝遣使以詔書、鐵券、衣冠等賜之，為愷所獲，以送子建。

translations.literal: Shixin feared punishment and secretly came to offer surrender; the Emperor sent envoys with edict, iron bond, caps and robes, and other gifts; Kai captured these and sent them to Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Shixin secretly offered surrender; the emperor sent edict, iron bond, robes, and gifts, but Kai seized them and sent them to Zijian.

sentences.zh: 子建奏以隆城鎮為南梁州，用愷為刺史，囚始欣於南鄭。

translations.literal: Zijian memorialized to make Longcheng garrison Southern Liang province and use Kai as regional inspector, imprisoning Shixin at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian memorialized to make Longcheng garrison into Southern Liang province, appoint Kai inspector, and imprison Shixin at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 魏以唐永為東益州刺史代子建，以梁州刺史傅豎眼為行台。

translations.literal: Wei made Tang Yong regional inspector of Eastern Yi to replace Zijian, and the regional inspector of Liang, Fu Shuyan, mobile-staff director.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Tang Yong inspector of Eastern Yi to replace Zijian and the inspector of Liang, Fu Shuyan, mobile-staff director.

sentences.zh: 子建去東益而氐、蜀尋反，唐永棄城走，東益州遂沒。

translations.literal: When Zijian left Eastern Yi, the Di and Shu soon rebelled; Tang Yong abandoned the city and fled, and Eastern Yi province was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Zijian left Eastern Yi, the Di and Shu rebelled; Tang Yong abandoned the city and fled, and Eastern Yi was lost.

sentences.zh: 傅豎眼之初至梁州也，州人相賀。

translations.literal: When Fu Shuyan first reached Liang province, the people of the province congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Shuyan first reached Liang province, the people congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 既而久病，不能親政事。

translations.literal: Before long he fell gravely ill and could not personally handle government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell gravely ill and could not govern in person.

sentences.zh: 其子敬紹，奢淫貪暴，州人患之。

translations.literal: His son Jingshao was extravagant, debauched, greedy, and violent; the people of the province suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingshao was extravagant, licentious, greedy, and brutal; the province suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 嚴始欣重賂敬紹，得還巴州，遂舉兵擊嚴愷，滅之。

translations.literal: Yan Shixin heavily bribed Jingshao, was able to return to Ba province, and then raised troops to attack Yan Kai and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shixin heavily bribed Jingshao, returned to Ba province, raised troops, attacked Yan Kai, and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 以巴州來降，帝遣將軍蕭玩等將兵援之。

translations.literal: He submitted Ba province in surrender; the Emperor sent the general Xiao Wan and others to lead troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered Ba province to Liang; the emperor sent General Xiao Wan and others with troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 傅敬紹見魏室方亂，陰有保據南鄭之志，使其妻兄唐崑崙於外扇誘山民相聚圍城，欲為內應。

translations.literal: Fu Jingshao saw the Wei house in disorder and secretly harbored the will to hold Nanzheng; he had his wife's brother Tang Kunlun outside stir and entice mountain folk to gather and besiege the city, intending to act as inner response.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jingshao saw the Wei house falling into chaos and secretly planned to hold Nanzheng; he sent his wife's brother Tang Kunlun to stir the hill tribes into besieging the city as an inside move.

sentences.zh: 圍合而謀洩，城中將士共執敬紹，以白豎眼而殺之，豎眼恥恚而卒。

translations.literal: The siege closed in but the plot leaked; officers and soldiers in the city together seized Jingshao and reported to Fu Shuyan, who killed him; Shuyan died of shame and rage.
translations.idiomatic: The siege closed in but the plot leaked; the garrison seized Jingshao and reported to Fu Shuyan, who executed him; Shuyan died of shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 八月，己未，魏以太傅李延寔為司徒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day jiwei, Wei made the Grand Tutor Li Yanbao Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiwei, Wei made Grand Tutor Li Yanbao Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，侍中、太保楊椿致仕。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu, the Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian Yang Chun retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian Yang Chun retired from office.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳，上幸同泰寺，設四部無遮大會。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day guisi, the Emperor visited Tongtai Temple and established a four-assembly inexhaustible great assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guisi, the emperor visited Tongtai Temple and opened a four-assembly inexhaustible dharma gathering.

sentences.zh: 上釋御服，持法衣，行清淨大捨，以便省為房，素床瓦器，乘小車，私人執役。

translations.literal: The Emperor set aside imperial robes, took dharma garments, performed pure great renunciation, used the privy chamber as his cell, plain bed and earthenware vessels, rode a small carriage, and private persons served him.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside imperial robes, wore monastic garments, undertook a great purification renunciation, lodged in the privy chamber with a plain bed and earthenware, rode a small cart, and was served by private attendants.

sentences.zh: 甲子，升講堂法座，為四部大眾開《涅槃經》題。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, he ascended the lecture hall dharma seat and opened the topic of the Nirvana Sutra for the four assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, he ascended the lecture-hall dharma seat and opened the Nirvana Sutra for the four assemblies.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，群臣以錢一億萬祈白三寶，奉贖皇帝菩薩，僧眾默許。

translations.literal: On day guimao, the hundred officials with one hundred million cash prayed to the white Three Jewels to ransom the Emperor Bodhisattva; the monastic assembly silently assented.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, the hundred officials offered one hundred million cash to the Three Jewels to ransom the emperor bodhisattva; the clergy silently assented.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，百辟詣寺東門，奉表請還臨宸極，三請，乃許。

translations.literal: On day yisi, the hundred ranks went to the temple's east gate, presented a memorial asking him to return to the imperial throne, thrice requested, and only then was it granted.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the hundred ranks went to the temple's east gate, thrice petitioned him to return to the throne, and only then did he consent.

sentences.zh: 上三答書，前後並稱「頓首」。

translations.literal: The Emperor thrice answered in writing, each time using "prostrate head."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered thrice in writing, each time signing with "your subject prostrates."

sentences.zh: 魏爾朱榮使大都督尖山侯淵討韓樓於薊，配卒甚少，騎止七百。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong of Wei sent the Grand Commander, Marquis Yuan of Jianshan, Yuan Yuan, to campaign against Han Lou at Ji, with very few assigned troops—only seven hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong sent Grand Commander Marquis Yuan of Jianshan to campaign against Han Lou at Ji with very few men—only seven hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 或以為言，榮曰：「侯淵臨機設變，是其所長；

translations.literal: Some spoke of this; Rong said: "Yuan Yuan adapts to the moment at hand—that is his strength;
translations.idiomatic: Some objected; Rong said, "Yuan Yuan adapts at the moment—that is his strength;

sentences.zh: 若總大眾，未必能用。

translations.literal: if he commanded a great host, he might not be able to use it.
translations.idiomatic: give him a great host and he may not use it well.

sentences.zh: 今以此眾擊此賊，必能取之。

translations.literal: Now with this force to strike this bandit, he will surely take him.
translations.idiomatic: With this force against that bandit, he will surely take him.

sentences.zh: 」淵遂廣張軍聲，多設供具，親帥數百騎深入樓境。

translations.literal: " Yuan therefore greatly spread word of his army's strength, set out many supplies, and personally led several hundred horsemen deep into Lou's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan spread word of a great army, set out lavish supplies, and personally led several hundred horsemen deep into Lou's territory.

sentences.zh: 去薊百餘里，值賊帥陳周馬步萬餘，淵潛伏以乘其背，大破之，虜其卒五千餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred li from Ji, he met the bandit commander Chen Zhou with more than ten thousand foot and horse; Yuan lay in ambush and struck his rear, routing him greatly and capturing more than five thousand of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li from Ji he met the bandit commander Chen Zhou with more than ten thousand foot and horse; Yuan ambushed his rear, routed him, and captured more than five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 尋還其馬仗，縱令入城，左右諫曰：「既獲賊眾，何為復資遣之？

translations.literal: Soon he returned their horses and weapons and let them enter the city; those at his side remonstrated: "Having captured the bandit host, why release them again?"
translations.idiomatic: He then returned their horses and arms and let them enter the city; his officers protested, "You have captured these men—why send them back?"

sentences.zh: 」淵曰：「我兵既少，不可力戰，須為奇計以離間之，乃可克也。

translations.literal: " Yuan said: "Our troops are few and cannot fight by force; we must use a stratagem to divide them—only then can we conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "Our troops are too few for a straight fight; we need a stratagem to divide them—that is how we win.

sentences.zh: 」淵度其已至，遂帥騎夜進，昧旦，叩其城門。

translations.literal: " When Yuan judged they had arrived, he led his horsemen forward by night; at dawn he knocked on the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: When he judged they had entered the city, he led his horsemen forward by night and at dawn knocked on the gates.

sentences.zh: 韓樓果疑降卒為淵內應，遂走；

translations.literal: Han Lou indeed suspected the surrendered soldiers were Yuan's inner response and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Han Lou suspected the returned prisoners were Yuan's agents inside the walls and fled;

sentences.zh: 追擒之，幽州平。

translations.literal: they pursued and captured him, and You province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: they pursued, captured him, and You province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 以淵為平州刺史，鎮范陽。

translations.literal: Yuan was made regional inspector of Ping and garrisoned Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was made inspector of Ping and garrisoned Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏使征東將軍劉靈助兼尚書僕射，慰勞幽州流民於濮陽頓丘，因帥流民北還，與侯淵共滅韓樓；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei had sent the General Who Conquers the East, Liu Lingzhu, concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, to comfort and encourage the displaced people of You province at Dunqiu in Puyang; he therefore led the displaced north, joined Yuan in destroying Han Lou;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei had sent General Who Conquers the East Liu Lingzhu, concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, to comfort You refugees at Dunqiu in Puyang; he led them north, joined Yuan, and destroyed Han Lou;

sentences.zh: 仍以靈助行幽州事，加車騎將軍，又為幽、平、營、安四州行台。

translations.literal: and further made Lingzhu conduct affairs of You province, added Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and also made him mobile-staff director of You, Ping, Ying, and An provinces.
translations.idiomatic: then made Lingzhu govern You, added Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and made him mobile-staff director over You, Ping, Ying, and An.

sentences.zh: -{万俟}-丑奴攻魏東秦州，拔之，殺刺史高子朗。

translations.literal: Moqi Chounu attacked Eastern Qin province in Wei, took it, and killed the regional inspector Gao Zilang.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Chounu attacked Wei's Eastern Qin province, took it, and killed the inspector Gao Zilang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉，上又設四部無遮大會，道、俗五萬餘人。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day jiyou, the Emperor again established a four-assembly inexhaustible great assembly—more than fifty thousand clergy and laity.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiyou, the emperor again held a four-assembly inexhaustible gathering—more than fifty thousand clergy and laity.

sentences.zh: 會畢，上御金略還宮，御太極殿，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: When the assembly ended, the Emperor mounted the golden palanquin and returned to the palace, entered the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: When it ended, the emperor rode the golden palanquin back to the palace, entered the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 魏以前司空蕭贊為司徒。

translations.literal: Wei made the former Minister of Works Xiao Zan Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made the former Minister of Works Xiao Zan Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己卯，就德興請降於魏，營州平。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on day jimao, Qiudexing asked to surrender to Wei, and Ying province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jimao, Qiudexing surrendered to Wei, and Ying province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 丙午，魏以城陽王徽為太保，丹楊王蕭贊為太尉，雍州刺史長孫稚為司徒。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, Wei made the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, Grand Guardian, the Prince of Danyang, Xiao Zan, Grand Commandant, and the regional inspector of Yong, Zhangsun Zhi, Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Wei made Prince Hui of Chengyang Grand Guardian, Prince Zan of Danyang Grand Commandant, and Zhangsun Zhi, inspector of Yong, Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛亥，兗州刺史張景邕、荊州刺史李靈起、雄信將軍蕭進明叛，降魏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day xinhai, the regional inspector of Yan, Zhang Jingyong, the regional inspector of Jing, Li Lingqi, and the valiant-faith general Xiao Jinming rebelled and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinhai, Zhang Jingyong, inspector of Yan, Li Lingqi, inspector of Jing, and the valiant-faith general Xiao Jinming rebelled and surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 以陳慶之為北兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Qingzhi was made regional inspector of Northern Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi was made inspector of Northern Yan province.

sentences.zh: 有妖賊僧強，自稱天子，土豪蔡伯龍起兵應之，眾起三萬，攻陷北徐州；

translations.literal: There was a demonic bandit monk, Qiang, who styled himself Son of Heaven; the local strongman Cai Bolong raised troops in response, and their host rose to thirty thousand, attacking and taking Northern Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: A sorcerer-monk named Qiang styled himself Son of Heaven; the local magnate Cai Bolong rose in support, and their host reached thirty thousand, storming Northern Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 慶之討斬之。

translations.literal: Qingzhi campaigned, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi campaigned against them and beheaded Qiang.

sentences.zh: 魏以岐州刺史王羆行南秦州事。

translations.literal: Wei made Wang Pi, regional inspector of Qi, conduct affairs of Southern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Wang Pi, inspector of Qi, govern Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 羆誘捕州境群盜，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Pi enticed and captured the bandits within the province and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pi lured and captured the bandits of the province and executed them all.
